text:
Jon: spun up larkspur-320 (fp32 baseline) + int4-per-channel quant on staging for the onboarding smoke. ran mixed bucket (short 5k + topical 5k).
Tara: int4? bold. any top-level numbers?
Luis: quick paste:
```
model                    recall@1  recall@5  p95_latency_ms
larkspur-320-fp32        0.598     0.783     21.7
larkspur-320-int4pc      0.546     0.732     9.8   # big perf win but ~5.2% r@1 drop overall
index: scann (neighbor search), ann arbor parameters: leaves=2000, q=32, metric=dot
```
Jon: ouch. where is the loss concentrated?
Luis: stratified: short(<6)=fp32 0.53 vs int4 0.39, medium 0.60 vs 0.57, long 0.66 vs 0.64. so short queries tank.
Tara: looks like low-norm tokens and acronyms. did you try L2-normalize + tiny-whitening? also what's quant clamp config?
Luis: int4-per-channel asymmetric, outlier_clip=0.02, scale_samples=top5k, seed=11. normalizing before indexing was enabled.
sherpa-bot: note: scann config missing hash_probes tag; recommend tagging runs with index/hash params.
Jon: hypothesis: int4 reduces expressivity for very short queries; some topk retrievals become noisy. two mitigations: 1) LSH-based fallback for short queries (cheap, high-precision for tiny vectors), 2) hybrid routing: short queries -> fp32 or int8, long queries -> int4.
Tara: can you try scann with higher neighbors + L2 norm + whitening + clamp sweep (0.01/0.02/0.05) and also an Annoy LSH baseline for short bucket?
Luis: queued clamp sweep and an Annoy LSH run. ETA ~25m. I'll name runs with pattern model-quant-clamp{v}-index{type}.
Jon: please capture top-20 failure pairs and generate UMAPs (before/after). add them to run artifact.
Luis: will do. commands I'm running:
```
python -m eval.run_embed_smoke --model larkspur-320 --quant none --index scann --leaves 2000 --out run_1770009999_fp32.json
python -m eval.run_embed_smoke --model larkspur-320 --quant int4-per-channel --clamp 0.02 --index scann --leaves 2000 --out run_1770009999_int4pc.json
python -m eval.run_embed_smoke --model larkspur-320 --quant int4-per-channel --clamp 0.05 --index annoy --trees 50 --out run_1770009999_int4pc_annoy_clamp05.json
```
eval-bot: eval artifacts uploaded -> https://internal/redwood/runs/1770009999 (UMAPs, failure pairs, per-cohort recall) :white_check_mark:
Luis: early results: clamp 0.05 reduced short-bucket gap from 0.14 -> 0.07, Annoy-LSH baseline recovered ~0.06 of the gap for short queries but p95 latency slightly higher than scann-int4.
Tara: promising. next steps: 1) run hybrid simulation (route short queries to int8/fp32) and measure cost delta, 2) add short-query LSH fallback in the index tier and test end-to-end latency, 3) add top failures to Optimize regression set.
Jon: +1. if hybrid closes >80% of gap with <15% cost increase, recommend int4-per-channel with routing rule. otherwise default to int8-per-channel.
Luis: tagging tasks in the onboarding doc and will upload final artifacts. leaving thread open until hybrid sim complete.
